newsitem.title: UK: NatWest has strong underlying profits.
newsitem.headline: NatWest has strong underlying profits.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc on Tuesday reported a 27 percent jump in underlying profit but said its headline profits figure was hit by one-off items.
Profit before tax was 1.12 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) after exceptional items, with operating profit from continuing operations up by 339 million to 1.61 billion pounds.
The bank said it expected the pace of UK economic growth to slow in 1998, however, and as a consequence was adopting a more cautious approach to lending.

"Although the UK economic environment remains positive, we see the pace of growth slowing in 1998 and are adopting a more cautious approach to lending," said NatWest chairman Lord Alexander in a statement.
Alexander said the markets in which NatWest operated were increasingly competitive, adding that the bank would make additional investment.
He said the year saw the culmination of the reshaping of NatWest, adding there was "much more to come" from its refocused portfolio of businesses.

The pre-tax profit figure came after a loss of 719 million pounds on sale of businesses such as its U.S. banking operation Bancorp, costs of 186 million on the redesign of its UK retail bank and a gain of 224 million on the sale of its stake in venture capital company 3i.
Alexander said its investment banking arm NatWest Markets had another year of real progress and "is rapidly establishing itself as a major force in investment banking'.
Pre-tax profits at NatWest Markets rose to 462 million pounds from 304 million, although this included a fall in bad debt provisions to 18 million pounds from 114 million.
Alexander said the bank saw no need for further acquisitions in this business and was focusing on organic growth and integration "to achieve our aim of becoming a premier investment bank".
Separately, NatWest chief executive Derek Wanless said the group would not bid in the auction currently under way for mutually-owned life insurer Scottish Amicable.
NatWest is paying a final dividend of 19.4 pence, raising the total for the year by 14.6 percent to 29.0p.
Analysts had forecast NatWest pretax profit at between 1.09 and 1.25 billion pounds. NatWest shares fell in early trading, being quoted down 23-1/2 pence at 789.
